newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK STATE UTILITY SIGNS 70MLN ECU LOAN WITH EIB.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK STATE UTILITY SIGNS 70MLN ECU LOAN WITH EIB.

text.p: Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. (SE), the Slovak state monopoly electricity utility, on Friday signed a 15-year, 70 million ECU loan with the European Investment Bank (EIB).
The loan will be priced as the facility is drawn at a level covering the EIB's costs for obtaining the credit, officials said at the signing ceremony.
The loan will be used for the refurbishment of a power plant at Vojany, eastern Slovakia.
Officials said the credit, with no state guarantees, is expected to be followed by another 65 million ECU tranche from EIB for the same project, planned for 1999 to 2002.
"This is the EIB's first non-sovereign guaratneed operation in the Slovak Republic," EIB vice-president Wolfgang Roth said after the signing ceremony.
"It (the loan) reflects the increasing interests of the international financial community in Slovakia, stemming from the strong performence of the country's economy in recent years," Roth said.

The credit, along with the seven-year 1.5 billion crown syndicated bond issue announced on Thursday, will increase the total debt financing the Slovak state monopoly power producer has received in 1996 to 50 billion crowns, SE officials said.
